items.Name: Yala
items.Tagline / One-liner: The best possible team to organize your seminars in France and abroad

items.Name: Playlist Studio
items.Description: A Brooklyn-based design studio that focuses on where brand, marketing, and digital products come together. From bold, large-scape initiatives to projects that help small businesses grow, our work is rooted in a deep appreciation for detail, creativity, and imagination.

items.Name: Victoria Heim
items.Description: I’m Victoria, a brand & digital designer based in Paris. I like to create colorful and accessible projects that merge art direction, branding, web design, and digital interactions. Here you’ll discover a selection of my work, hope you’ll enjoy it!

items.Name: Apron
items.Tagline / One-liner: Sort your business money, in and out
items.Description: Apron helps businesses manage payments, expenses, and cash flow. Capture invoices, issue expense cards, pay suppliers and employees, and get paid—all in one platform with seamless accounting integrations.

items.Name: Metalab
items.Description: Founded in British Columbia, we’ve always hired the best talent we could find from every corner of the world. We believe giving our teams the autonomy to work whenever, wherever they want delivers the best outcomes.

items.Name: Source
items.Tagline / One-liner: Founded in 2014, Source.paris is a Bureau of Design & Technology.

items.Name: Article
items.Tagline / One-liner: Brand and Digital for Culture, Commerce and Good.
items.Description: We’re a full-service digital agency building better brands for the emerging & established. With our team’s expertise, we blend the science of user experience with the art of visual design.

items.Name: Field
items.Tagline / One-liner: A global design and innovation practice based in London and Berlin, where we are shaping intelligent spaces, experiences, and products.

items.Name: Moxie Strategies
items.Tagline / One-liner: A national boutique public affairs firm specializing in bold, transformative impact for brands and causes that aim to stand out.

items.Name: Camila Rosa
items.Description: I create artwork that invites reflection on feminism, social justice, and identity. I use illustration as a tool to challenge perspectives, celebrate diversity, and promote inclusivity. My work includes projects in advertising, editorial, fashion, beauty, and graphic design, always aligning with my values.

items.Name: Julian Lehr
items.Description: Personal writing + reflections: “A digital image or map of my life. Pictures I take, thoughts I have, things I find.

items.Name: Daniël van der Winden
items.Description: My home on the internet, primarily dedicated to my hobbies, filled with what I read, watch, find, and am focused on now.

items.Name: Andrés Briganti
items.Bio: Andrés Briganti is a designer specializing in brand identity and the visual systems that support it. He works across editorial design, digital experiences, and custom typefaces to deliver clear, cohesive communication for brands.

items.Name: Noël Leu
items.Bio:
Noël Leu was born 1984 in Lucerne, Switzerland. In 2010 he graduated with a Bachelor in Visual Commu- nication from the Bern University of Arts. He now lives and works in the whole world as a graphic designer, teacher and curator. He co-founded Edition Grilli, an independent pub- lishing house and Grilli Type GmbH, a digital type foundry.

Noël Leu is a graphic designer and co-founder of the Swiss based type foundry Grilli Type. He usually spends a large part of the year traveling the globe to broaden his horizon, getting inspired, and to give lectures about design.

items.Name: Caio Kondo
items.Bio: A Brazilian-Japanese type designer hailing from São Paulo. His journey in typography has been a captivating one, marked by a fusion of his dual heritage and a relentless pursuit of excellence in design.

items.Name: Robin Nicholas
items.Current Role: Head of Typography at Monotype Imaging

items.Name: Steve Matteson
items.Bio:
A type designer who loves bringing letters to life—whether it means creating fonts for cutting-edge digital platforms or reviving timeless designs from typography’s rich history.

My experiences range from designing Microsoft’s Aptos and Google’s Open Sans fonts to building custom brand fonts for Toyota, Xbox, Unilever, and others. I stay connected to the tradition and craft of type through letterpress printing and typographic education.

Typography is my passion. Whether I’m reviving historical designs or creating fonts for today’s most cutting-edge applications, I strive to craft letterforms that connect and communicate.

items.Name: Jelle Bosma
items.Bio:
Jelle Bosma (b. Rijswijk, The Netherlands, 1959) studied at the Royal Academy of Art in The Hague and. like many of his contemporaries, was influenced by Gerrit Noordzij. He works from a studio near The Hadue, and designs type, programs font tools, hints, and produces type. His typefaces:

He created WTC Cursivium (1986, World Typeface Center).
He was one of the main type designers at Scangraphic from 1988-1991, where he designed Forlane in 1991.
Bosma joined Monotype in 1992. His role was to oversee TrueType® production and hinting. One of Bosma's first projects for the company's UK office was to manage the production of Greek and Cyrillic core fonts for the Windows® 3.1 operating system. Known for his work with non-Latin typefaces, Bosma has produced fonts for Hebrew, Thai, Arabic and Indic scripts. He relies a lot on his own software, including a truetype font editor called FontDame. He also claims that there are no more than 25 professional hinters world-wide. Alternate URL.
Bosma was part of the team that developed corporate identity typefaces for Nokia. Launched in 2002, the Nokia types include sans, serif, and bitmap versions in varying weights. The Nokia fonts are used for everything from architectural signage and printed brochures to screen type for phones and other devices.
In 2004, he created the OpenType family Cambria for Microsoft's ClearType project.

The Nokia fonts are used for everything from architectural signage and printed brochures to screen type for phones and other devices.

items.Name: Mark Bloom
items.Bio:
I have close to 20 years of design experience specialising in brand identity and packaging design. During this time I have worked with some of the world’s leading design studios, producing logos and typefaces for major global brands and agencies.

I work with clients of all sizes and from various sectors, both locally and internationally. I pride myself in providing innovative, unique design solutions that add value to my clients’ brands. It is my aim to form long term business relationships with all my clients, delivering design work that will deliver over and above expectations.

items.Name: Nolan Paparelli
items.Bio: Nolan Paparelli is a Swiss graphic and type designer currently based in Munich, Germany. Originally from the french-speaking part of Switzerland, he graduated with a Bachelor in Graphic design at ECAL in 2015 and officially runs his own independent practice since 2017. Through the years, in parallel of developing his personal work, he collaborated with the likes of Swiss Typefaces, Herburg Weiland and Think Work Observe to name a few. In 2021, his typeface Everett has been published by WELTKERN®, a type foundry with which he is closely associated. His work focuses mainly in the fields of editorial design, visual identity, web and type design with a strong sense of detail and particular attention to typography.

items.Name: Selma Losch
items.Bio: Selma Losch is a Berlin based type designer. She earned an MA in Typeface Design from the University of Reading. In London, she gained experience developing fonts for international clients. Selma's mission is to create beautiful and functional typefaces that resonate with diverse audiences.

items.Name: Maggie Moran
items.Bio: Maggie Moran, Founder and CEO of Moxie Strategies, is a trailblazing public affairs leader with an unparalleled reputation for delivering bold, results-driven strategies. As the founder of two award-winning public affairs firms, Maggie has redefined external affairs through her expertise in strategy development, corporate communications, public affairs campaign management, labor relations, brand management, and external affairs.
items.Current Role: Founder and CEO of Moxie Strategies

items.Name: Rasmus Andersson
items.Bio: My name is Rasmus Andersson. I’m a Swedish he/him living in San Francisco, California. Software is the medium through which I express myself.

items.Name: Suisse Int’l
items.Description: The Suisse typeface forms the centerpiece of the Swiss Typefaces library. Comprised of 6 collections with a total of 55 styles, Suisse is a utilitarian font set that covers all basic needs of the contemporary typographer, from Suisse Int’l, the go-to Grotesk with its monospaced and condensed companions, to the sturdy text serif Suisse Works, the clear-cut sans serif Suisse Screen, and the reliable slab serif Suisse Neue. Suisse combines classic style with cutting edge design quality and the most user-friendly license.

items.Name: Monument Grotesk
items.Overview: ABC Monument Grotesk owes its point de départ to a few intriguing contours that the Swiss design studio Kasper-Florio stumbled across in an online scan of the foundry Palmer & Rey’s 1884 New Specimen Book. Compelled by the letterforms’ compact skeleton, high vertical contrast, and surprisingly sharp end strokes, Kasper-Florio digitized and reinterpreted the typeface for contemporary use. Ever since, the design has served as the studio’s house typeface, and it’s been available to the public via Dinamo since 2018.

items.Name: TEG
items.Overview: TEG™ is a modern sans-serif, merging geometric and grotesque features through its even stroke weight and a blend of sharp and rounded details, creating a futuristic-classic grotesque impression.

items.Name: Geist Mono
items.Description:
Geist had to echo the greatness of legendary typefaces like Univers, SF Mono, SF Pro, Inter, and Suisse International.

The letterforms of Geist are characterized by several key features, including a high x-height that enhances legibility across a range of sizes. Additionally, the design incorporates short descenders, along with angular strokes on specific terminals, elbows, and descender strokes, contributing to its distinct and functional appearance.

items.Name: Basis Grotesque
items.Description: The Basis Grotesque Font Family was designed by Jelle Bosma, Steve Matteson, Robin Nicholas, Colophon Foundry and published by Colophon Foundry. Basis Grotesque contains 16 styles and family package options.
items.Type Designer Fallback: Jelle Bosma, Steve Matteson, Robin Nicholas

items.Name: Figtree
items.Description: Figtree is a geometric sans serif font walking the line between simplicity and friendliness. It is minimalist but not stiff, casual but not silly.

items.Name: EB Garamond
items.Description: Garamond’s fonts represent a milestone in the history of type design, a touchstone to which font designers have been returning ever since. EB Garamond is an open source project to create a revival of Claude Garamond’s famous humanist typeface from the mid-16th century. Its design reproduces the original by Claude Garamont.

items.Name: Lausanne
items.Description: Designed as a modern response to historical sans-serifs like Helvetica, Lausanne brings a contemporary edge shaped by the possibilities of digital typography. This includes the duality and adaptability of distinct "Text" and "Display" styles, ensuring optimal performance across different contexts. Its compact appearance, achieved through short ascenders and descenders, adds to its clean and structured feel, making it as functional as it is elegant.

items.Name: Aeonik
items.Description:
Aeonik is a versatile workhorse type family, crafted with mechanical precision by Mark Bloom and Joe Leadbeater. Conceived as a “neo-grotesque with a geometric skeleton,” it delivers rigidity in its strict perpendicular terminals – most evident in the letters ‘a, ‘t,’ ‘f,’ and ‘j.’ This is offset by the geometric roundness of letters like ‘c,’ ‘e,’  and ‘o,’. The balance between mechanical precision and timeless aesthetics has resonated with designers since its launch in 2021.

Aeonik excels in large-scale applications such as logotypes and headlines, while also performing seamlessly in longer bodies of text. Its versatile weights and extensive character set make it ideal for creating cohesive and enduring brand identities. Aeonik’s widespread use by brands like Revolut, Eurosport, Alipay, and Virgin Hyperloop is a testament to its adaptability and timeless appeal.
items.Highlights: Aeonik is a versatile workhorse type family, crafted with mechanical precision by Mark Bloom and Joe Leadbeater. Conceived as a “neo-grotesque with a geometric skeleton,” it delivers rigidity in its strict perpendicular terminals – most evident in the letters ‘a, ‘t,’ ‘f,’ and ‘j.’ This is offset by the geometric roundness of letters like ‘c,’ ‘e,’  and ‘o,’. The balance between mechanical precision and timeless aesthetics has resonated with designers since its launch in 2021.

items.Name: Maison Neue Mono
items.Description: The Maison Font Family was designed by Timo Gaessner and published by Milieu Grotesque. Maison contains 20 styles and family package options.

items.Name: Whyte
items.Description: ABC Whyte is a contemporary grotesque typeface filled with idiosyncrasies and character, and it’s available as two distinctive subfamilies. ABC Whyte has smooth and sharp transitions, while ABC Whyte Inktrap has ink traps at its joints. Ink traps were necessary during the hot metal type printing era, in order to improve the quality of printed text. Using variable font technology, users are able to deepen or shorten the ink traps of this typeface for the first time, sliding from deep wells to shorter cuts. In doing so, Whyte transforms something once functional into a beautiful design detail in its own right.
items.Type Designer Fallback: Fabian Harb & Johannes Breyer, with Erkin Karamemet & Fabiola Mejía

items.Name: Roobert
items.Overview:
Roobert is a mono-linear, geometric sans-serif typeface characterized by its clean, horizontal and  vertical terminals, and smooth connections on the stems. Originally crafted as a custom typeface for Moogfest 2017, Roobert draws its foundational inspiration from the Moog logotype, notably its unique single-story “g” with a rounded bottom corner and a streamlined finish. This inspiration is evident in the typeface’s distinct “bent pipe” feature, observed in the comma and ingeniously echoed throughout the entire typeface.

Named in homage to Robert Moog, the American engineer, electronic music pioneer, and founder of Moog Music, Roobert carries the legacy of its namesake, who was renowned for his groundbreaking invention, the Moog synthesizer, and his contributions to the field of electronic music instruments.

items.Name: Martina Plantijn
items.Description: Martina Plantijn is a better Plantin. Informed by the workhorse qualities of Frank Hinman Pierpont’s typeface and expanding upon his research of 16th century type at the Plantin-Moretus Museum in Antwerp, Martina Plantijn makes decisive digital updates across its roman and italic cuts.

items.Name: Mānuka
items.Description: Mānuka is a collection of compressed fonts for large sizes. With deviant details pilfered from Teutonic timber type, Mānuka grafts a contemporary antipodean aesthetic onto 19th century German root-stock. Tight spacing, closed apertures and sharp joins make a compelling texture, like sunlight sparkling through a forest canopy.

items.Name: Champ
items.Description: Champ is a versatile sans serif typeface that brings fun and friendliness to your designs. With its cheerful and approachable personality, it is the ideal choice for brand materials, logotypes, and websites. Available in 9 weights, Champ offers a range of options for any project, from headlines to body text. Whether you're looking to create bold, impactful designs or subtle, nuanced typography, Champ has you covered. And with the variable file included in the full family pack, you have the flexibility to customize and personalize your designs to match your unique style and aesthetic.

items.Name: Söhne
items.Description: Söhne is the memory of Akzidenz-Grotesk framed through the reality of Helvetica. It captures the analogue materiality of “Standard Medium” used in Unimark’s legendary wayfinding system for the NYC Subway.

items.Name: Geist
items.Description:
Geist had to echo the greatness of legendary typefaces like Univers, SF Mono, SF Pro, Inter, and Suisse International.

The letterforms of Geist are characterized by several key features, including a high x-height that enhances legibility across a range of sizes. Additionally, the design incorporates short descenders, along with angular strokes on specific terminals, elbows, and descender strokes, contributing to its distinct and functional appearance.

items.Name: Eiko
items.Overview: Eiko is an indisputable statement of elegance and refinement. Every curves and bezier points were applied with a sense of purpose. It is inspired by the work of Eiko Ishioka, a multitalented Japanese artist, this typeface seeks to convey the same aspect of her work in these typographic explorations. It is an original serif font with high contrast, including the syllable alphabet kana, hiragana & katakana, it is ideal to pair with other kanji fonts of the Japanese mincho style.
items.Description: Eiko is an indisputable statement of elegance and refinement ● Every curves and bezier points were applied with a sense of purpose. It is inspired by the work of Eiko Ishioka, a multitalented Japanese artist, this typeface seeks to convey the same aspect of her work in these typographic explorations ■ It is an original serif font with high contrast, including the syllable alphabet kana, hiragana & katakana, it is ideal to pair with other kanji fonts of the Japanese mincho style.

items.Name: GT America
items.Description: GT America is the missing bridge between 19th century American Gothics and 20th century European Neo-Grotesk typefaces. It uses the best design features from both traditions in the widths and weights where they function optimally.

items.Name: Everett
items.Description: Everett emerged during Nolan Paparelli’s studies at ECAL/University of Art & Design Lausanne, resulting in his diploma work, and has been evolving ever since. Initially inspired by the work of the American photographer Daniel Everett, it quickly became more personal and resulted in his own take on the neogrotesque genre.

items.Name: Rhymes
items.Description:
Rhymes, Maxitype’s first serif typeface available for retail, was drawn between 2017 and 2021 by the Czech designer Jakub Samek.

Rhymes is a contemporary synthesis of the original, undigitised Times New Roman (Monotype, 48p, Series 327) [1] and another undigitised derivation, Times Book. Rather than a strict redesign, it’s a rhyme, drawing on the untapped potential of the early Times typeface. It comprises two distinct families: Rhymes Display and Rhymes Text. The whole composes a versatile and contemporary typeface offering a range of eight weights with their corresponding italics. On the one hand, the Display styles have greater contrast and finer details, with the shorter outer serifs on the diagonal strokes helping to create a tight and balanced spacing between characters. On the other, the Text styles feature several changes in proportions, lower contrast and slightly wider spacing. 

Rhymes has been tested and refined for screen: with the optical correction variable axis, users can adjust its contrast and serifs to let the font perform at its best across all resolutions and media.

items.Name: GT Walsheim
items.Description: Inspired by the lettering of Swiss poster designer legend Otto Baumberger from the 1930s, GT Walsheim is a friendly but precise typeface. Supports all Cyrillic languages.

items.Name: DM Sans
items.Description:
DM Sans is a low-contrast geometric sans serif design, intended for use at smaller text sizes.

DM Sans supports a Latin Extended glyph set, enabling typesetting for English and other Western European languages. It was designed by Colophon Foundry (UK), who started from the Latin portion of Indian Type Foundry's Poppins.

In May 2023 DM Sans is updated, expanding the coverage of the weight range to Thin & ExtraBlack (100–1000 weight range) along with a new optical size axis.

items.Name: Queens
items.Description: Generous, Confident, Adaptive. Such is the realm of Queens and its many different faces. As the layout gets narrower, Queens commands the letters to follow. And they obey, for they have three distinct widths (Compressed, Condensed, Standard) for the most flexible of applications. Not relying on a particular historical reference point, Queens’ lineage can be traced back to the Bodonis & Didots – inheriting some of the classical elegance, but renouncing the rigid mannerist construction in favor of playfulness.

items.Name: Apercu
items.Description: Drawing of Aperçu began in December 2009, and was tried & tested throughout a number of design commissions. Aperçu aimed to create a synopsis or amalgamation of classic realist typefaces: Johnston, Gill Sans, Neuzeit & Franklin Gothic into a contemporary flavor. A sum of parts from the outset, Aperçu builds upon these initial reference points to create an extensive and usable family.

items.Name: Inter
items.Overview: Designed for impactful Headings & effortless body readability.
items.Description:
Inter is a variable font family carefully crafted & designed for computer screens.

Inter features a tall x-height to aid in readability of mixed-case and lower-case text. Several OpenType features are provided as well, like contextual alternates that adjusts punctuation depending on the shape of surrounding glyphs, slashed zero for when you need to disambiguate "0" from "o", tabular numbers, etc.

The Inter project is led by Rasmus Andersson, a Swedish maker–of–software living in San Francisco. To contribute, see github.com/rsms/inter
items.Highlights:
Inter is a typeface designed specifically for screens, making it highly readable in digital environments. Its tall x-height ensures that lowercase letters appear larger and clearer, especially on small displays. With high optical balance, open counters, and clean curves, it maintains excellent legibility across sizes.

Inter is also available as a variable font, offering fine control over weight, width, and optical size, making it adaptable for diverse design needs. Combined with its neutral yet modern tone, wide language support, and open-source nature, Inter has become one of the most reliable choices for digital products, interfaces, and web design.
items.Use Case: Best suited for UI, Digital Products, and Web Content.
items.Q 1: What is the best line height and leading for paragraphs in Inter?
items.A 1: For body text, use a line height (leading) of 120–145% of the font size. This creates comfortable spacing for paragraphs and ensures smooth readability across digital and print.
items.Q 2: Where might Inter fall short compared to more geometric fonts like Avenir or Futura?
items.A 2: Optical size in Inter adjusts letterforms for readability at different sizes—wider, more open shapes for small text, and sharper, refined details for headings or larger display text.
items.Q 3: Is Inter neutral enough for corporate branding, or does it feel too technical?
items.A 3: Inter strikes a balance: neutral and professional for corporate branding but with a slight technical edge. It works well for tech companies, startups, and digital-first brands, but may feel too minimal for luxury or fashion.
items.Q 4: Does Inter work better for web apps or print materials?
items.A 4: Inter is designed for digital use apps, dashboards, websites. Its clarity also suits print in manuals, reports, and corporate documents. For editorial magazines or expressive print, a serif or display font may be better.
items.Q 5: What are the best kerning and tracking settings for Inter?
items.A 5: Inter’s kerning is finely tuned and best left at default. For tracking, use 0 to +2 for paragraphs, and slightly higher (+4 to +6) for all-caps text or headings to improve clarity.
items.Q 6: Can Inter replace system fonts like SF Pro or Segoe UI in interfaces?
items.A 6: Yes, Inter can effectively replace system fonts, especially in cross-platform apps where consistency matters. It provides a similar neutral tone but with better open shapes and readability, making it a reliable substitute.
items.Q 7: How does Inter handle numbers in dashboards compared to other sans fonts?
items.A 7: Inter includes tabular figures (tnum) & consistent numeral design, making it excellent for data tables, dashboards, & financial interfaces. Its clear, balanced numerals ensure numbers align neatly and stay legible at small sizes.
items.Q 8: Is Inter better suited for minimalist design systems or expressive ones?
items.A 8: Inter shines in minimalist, functional design systems where clarity and neutrality are key. In expressive systems, it can serve as a strong base font, but often needs a more playful or decorative companion typeface for balance.
items.Design Features:
• Tall x-height for readability

  • Open counters and clean curves

  • High optical balance for screen clarity

  • Neo-Grotesque sans serif style

  • Neutral, professional tone with subtle friendliness

items.Name: Blanco
items.Description: Blanco is a serif typeface with 4 weights designed primarily for comfortable, extended reading at smaller text sizes on screen and in print. Its strong, consistent rhythm creates an even value and texture that gives text blocks a calm tone of voice. The unfussy, sturdy details provide a contemporary, understated and thoughtful character. This character allows it to be easily paired with other typefaces, making it a versatile addition (or beginning) to a type library as a utilitarian face. While there are optical corrections in the forms to make Blanco work effectively at smaller sizes, these corrections remain unobtrusive at larger sizes, revealing a warmth and consideration to the details of the design.

items.Name: Roboto Mono
items.Description:
Roboto Mono is a monospaced addition to the Roboto type family. Like the other members of the Roboto family, the fonts are optimized for readability on screens across a wide variety of devices and reading environments. While the monospaced version is related to its variable width cousin, it doesn’t hesitate to change forms to better fit the constraints of a monospaced environment. For example, narrow glyphs like ‘I’, ‘l’ and ‘i’ have added serifs for more even texture while wider glyphs are adjusted for weight. Curved caps like ‘C’ and ‘O’ take on the straighter sides from Roboto Condensed.

Special consideration is given to glyphs important for reading and writing software source code. Letters with similar shapes are easy to tell apart. Digit ‘1’, lowercase ‘l’ and capital ‘I’ are easily differentiated as are zero and the letter ‘O’. Punctuation important for code has also been considered. For example, the curly braces ‘{ }’ have exaggerated points to clearly differentiate them from parenthesis ‘( )’ and braces ‘[ ]’. Periods and commas are also exaggerated to identify them more quickly. The scale and weight of symbols commonly used as operators have also been optimized.

items.Name: Degular
items.Description: From the foundry that → brought you, “Hobeaux” (2015), “Ohno™ Blazeface” (2019), and “Cheee” (2020), comes something with (significantly) less allure. ✨ While {most of} the fonts around here scream in desperate need of your peepers’ gaze, Degular aims to fade into the background [like the finest Japanese-made white noise machine as you drift off to ~dreamland~]. ¶ Degular also provides a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to use an Ohno font more than once! 7 weights, 3 optical sizes, in ☑roman and ☑italic.

items.Name: Colophon
items.Description: Colophon is an award-winning international type foundry based in London. Colophon is recognized for its custom typeface designs, library, creative team, and font technology tools. Colophon has created custom typographic assets for world-recognized brands including Burger King, Canva Sans, Cadillac, Twickenham, and Central Saint Martins. The Colophon library consists of new classics that feel both historically rooted and contemporary including Aperçu, Basis Grotesque, Fann Grotesque, Fortescue, Value Sans, and Value Serif.

items.Name: CoType
items.Description:
CoType is the London based type foundry of Mark Bloom and Co.

We design contemporary typefaces for use in digital and print applications. In addition to our retail offerings, we also offer design of bespoke typefaces and modifications of our existing font library.

All of our typefaces support Latin Extended-A, Western European, Central European & Southeastern European languages. We also offer across our entire font library, allowing you to try before you buy.

items.Name: ABC Dinamo
items.Description: Dinamo Typefaces is an independent type design studio based in Berlin. From our studio, we develop fonts, books, and other physical things—sometimes on our own, often in collaboration with our global network of contributors. Dinamo Typefaces moves fluidly between commercial and cultural projects of all shapes and sizes.

items.Name: Displaay Type Foundry
items.Description:
Displaay is an independent type foundry established in 2014 and based in Prague, Czech Republic. Our team has numerous collaborators around the world.

The foundry focuses on retail and custom typefaces. The aim is to develop distinctive typefaces that are missing on the market. Specific moments of imperfection and spontaneous irregularities inspire our ethos.

items.Name: Typeverything
items.Description: Typeverything is a type-foundry specialising in the development of display fonts. Founded in 2011 by Andrei Robu, the foundry brings together a collective of independent type designers focusing on creating the finest fonts for your projects. Typeverything has earned the trust of top studios and renowned brands around the world, whether you're working on branding, advertisements, or digital experiences, we are here to support you with the right tools.

items.Name: Klim Type Foundry
items.Description:
Klim Type Foundry (Klim) was founded by Kris Sowersby in 2005 and is based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara/Wellington, Aotearoa/New Zealand.

Our foundational ethos is “a thing well made”. Our typefaces combine historical knowledge with rigorous contemporary craft. We believe the alphabet is a concept made concrete through written and designed letterforms — the alphabet is not defined by a single typeface but expressed through all of them.

items.Name: Pangram Pangram
items.Description: Where the art of typography meets unparalleled craftsmanship. Established in 2018 by designer Mat Desjardins, Pangram Pangram has swiftly risen to become a globally recognized independent type foundry, admired and trusted by industry peers and the design community alike.

items.Name: Weltkern
items.Description: WELTKERN®, pronounced [velt-kern], is a Swiss-based, tech-driven company redefining design as a cultural cornerstone. Built on the belief that design is essential to human expression, WELTKERN® creates a unique ecosystem where luxury meets accessibility. With a curated selection of timeless, collectible objects and innovative digital experiences, WELTKERN® brings together the worlds of design, art, and culture.

items.Name: Swiss Typefaces
items.Description: We are a type design company known for our cutting-edge approach. Our typefaces are valued for their high quality, both in terms of aesthetics and technology. Every aspect of what we do is informed by our attitude to innovate.

items.Name: Grilli Type
items.Description: Noël Leu and Thierry Blancpain founded Grilli Type in Switzerland in late 2009 as a collaborative avenue for working with other designers. Although the foundry is based in Lucerne, we’re active on a global scale. Thierry now lives in New York City, and Noël travels extensively, ricocheting between East Asia, North America, and Europe. The studio now numbers eight, with colleagues dispersed across the globe.

items.Name: Kilotype
items.Description: Kilotype is an independent type publisher. In addition to our font catalogue we develop custom solutions for commercial and institutional clients. Extensive language support and a high production standard are essential to every typeface from Kilotype. Made in Germany, exclusively available from kilotype.de

items.Name: Colophon Foundry
items.Description: Colophon is an award-winning international type foundry based in London. Colophon is recognized for its custom typeface designs, library, creative team, and font technology tools. Colophon has created custom typographic assets for world-recognized brands including Burger King, Canva Sans, Cadillac, Twickenham, and Central Saint Martins. The Colophon library consists of new classics that feel both historically rooted and contemporary including Aperçu, Basis Grotesque, Fann Grotesque, Fortescue, Value Sans, and Value Serif.
